The final step is inference:
@dobson4e [§2.3.5] lists [confidence intervals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval),
[hypothesis tests](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#sec-hypothesis-tests) about the parameters,
and interpretation of the results.
By [the central limit theorem for MLEs](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#thm-dist-mle),
in large samples $\eb$ is approximately Gaussian,
with covariance matrix approximated by the inverse of the [observed information](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-oinf)
$-\hessf{\eb}$.
A 95% [Wald confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-wald-ci) for $\beta_j$ is then
$\eb_j \pm 1.96 \cdot \eSEf{\eb_j}$,
and the [Wald statistic](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-wald-test) $z_j \eqdef \eb_j / \eSEf{\eb_j}$
tests $H_0: \beta_j = 0$.

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-chronic-inference}
#### Comparing town and country women

In @exm-chronic-mle, the fitted means sum to
$\sum_{i:\, x_i = 0} \est{\mu}_i = n_{\text{town}} \bar{y}_{\text{town}} = 37$
for the town women
and
$\sum_{i:\, x_i = 1} \est{\mu}_i = n_{\text{country}} \bar{y}_{\text{country}} = 21$
for the country women.
Substituting into the Hessian from @exm-chronic-concavity,
the [observed information matrix](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-oinf) is

$$
\ba
\underbrace{-\hessf{\eb}}_{2 \times 2}
&= \sum_{i=1}^{49} \est{\mu}_i \pmat{1 & x_i \\ x_i & x_i^2}
&& \text{(Hessian of the log-likelihood)}
\\
&= \pmat{
  \sum_{i} \est{\mu}_i & \sum_{i:\, x_i = 1} \est{\mu}_i \\
  \sum_{i:\, x_i = 1} \est{\mu}_i & \sum_{i:\, x_i = 1} \est{\mu}_i
}
&& \text{(} x_i \in \{0, 1\} \text{, so } x_i^2 = x_i \text{)}
\\
&= \underbrace{\pmat{58 & 21 \\ 21 & 21}}_{2 \times 2}
&& \text{(} 37 + 21 = 58 \text{)}
\ea
$$

Its [determinant](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-determinant) is $58 \cdot 21 - 21 \cdot 21 = 21 \cdot 37 = 777$,
so its inverse is

$$
\ba
\underbrace{\sb{-\hessf{\eb}}^{-1}}_{2 \times 2}
&= \frac{1}{777} \pmat{21 & -21 \\ -21 & 58}
&& \text{(inverse of a } 2 \times 2 \text{ matrix)}
\ea
$$

The lower-right entry is the estimated variance of $\eb_1$:

$$
\ba
\eVar{\eb_1}
&= \frac{58}{777}
\\
&= \frac{37 + 21}{37 \cdot 21}
&& \text{(} 58 = 37 + 21 \text{, } 777 = 37 \cdot 21 \text{)}
\\
&= \frac{1}{21} + \frac{1}{37}
&& \text{(distribute the division over the sum, then cancel the common factors)}
\\
&\approx 0.0746
\ea
$$

so $\eSEf{\eb_1} \approx \sqrt{0.0746} \approx 0.2732$.

```{r}
#| label: chronic-inference
se_b1 <- sqrt(1 / 21 + 1 / 37)
ci_b1 <- b1_hat + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * se_b1
z_b1 <- b1_hat / se_b1
p_b1 <- 2 * pnorm(-abs(z_b1))
summary(chronic_glm)$coefficients
```

- The 95% Wald confidence interval for $\beta_1$ is
  from `r round(ci_b1[1], 3)` to `r round(ci_b1[2], 3)`.
- Exponentiating the estimate and the interval endpoints,
  the estimated ratio of the country mean to the town mean is
  $\expf{\eb_1} \approx$ `r round(exp(b1_hat), 3)`,
  with 95% confidence interval
  from `r round(exp(ci_b1[1]), 3)` to `r round(exp(ci_b1[2]), 3)`.
- The Wald statistic is
  $z \approx$ `r round(z_b1, 3)`,
  with two-sided [$p$-value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-p-value) $\approx$ `r round(p_b1, 3)`.

These hand calculations match the standard error, $z$ value, and $p$-value
that `summary()` reports for `country`.
On average, country women in this sample reported
`r round(100 * (1 - exp(b1_hat)))`% fewer chronic conditions
than town women,
but the confidence interval for the ratio includes 1,
so these data are also consistent with no difference in the mean number of conditions.
:::
